reference: man-db apropos is the independent CLI oracle for no-argument and version comparisons. Query parity requires man-db configuration unavailable in this runner. Private whatis searches use independently specified substring, anchored-name and AND contracts; these are not man-db query parity.
coverage: Parity for GNU apropos no-argument and version invocations, both of which run without search-path initialization.
Documented literal substring search over a relative private whatis fixture.
Documented -w matching at the head of an entry name, including a comma-separated alias.
Documented AND behavior across multiple patterns.
Documented nonzero outcomes for no matches and a missing whatis index.
Bash type/help metadata contract, counted separately from operation coverage.
exclusions: True GNU query comparisons are deferred because man-db exits with a configuration error in this runner before reading any query fixture.
Binary man-db index creation/refresh, other man-db options, locale-specific matching, and pager behavior are outside this suite.

cases.purpose: Compares no-argument invocation status and output. man-db documents status 1 for syntax errors; the candidate's usage path remains a parity comparison even if it differs.
Compare version stdout bytes and status directly with man-db; implementation identity differences remain visible.
Checks the documented default substring search against hand-written index records; every printed line contains the literal term in its name or description.
cases.script:
export MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1
printf '%s\n' 'alpha (1) - primary command' 'alphabet (1) - a longer name' 'beta (1) - mentions alpha in its summary' > whatis
apropos alpha
cases.stdout:
alpha (1) - primary command
alphabet (1) - a longer name
beta (1) - mentions alpha in its summary

cases.purpose: Checks the documented -w anchored name match: alpha matches exactly, while alpha-x is a near-prefix and beta is unrelated.
cases.script:
export MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1
printf '%s\n' 'alpha (1) - base page' 'alpha-x (1) - derived page' 'beta (1) - unrelated helper' > whatis
apropos -w alpha

cases.purpose: Checks that -w can select an exact alias name from the documented comma-separated whatis entry format.
cases.script:
export MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1
printf '%s\n' 'alpha, aleph (1) - an alphabetic symbol' 'beta (1) - unrelated helper' > whatis
apropos -w aleph

cases.purpose: Checks the documented AND contract across patterns: only the record containing both terms is printed.
cases.script:
export MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1
printf '%s\n' 'alpha (1) - first entry' 'both (1) - alpha and beta together' 'beta (1) - second entry' > whatis
apropos alpha beta

cases.purpose: Checks the documented nonzero result for a valid query with no matches without assuming a GNU-specific numeric status.
cases.script:
export MANPATH=. BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1
printf '%s\n' 'alpha (1) - ordinary command' 'beta (1) - helper command' > whatis
if apropos nofixturetoken; then exit 90; else rc=$?; [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; fi
printf '%s\n' 'no-match returns nonzero'

cases.purpose: Checks the documented nonzero result and diagnostic when the MANPATH contains no whatis index.
cases.script:
export MANPATH=missing BASHMAN_STALE_QUIET=1
if apropos alpha; then exit 90; else rc=$?; [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; fi
printf '%s\n' 'missing-index returns nonzero'

cases.purpose: Checks Bash builtin registration and help availability; this is metadata coverage, not apropos operation coverage.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t apropos) == builtin ]]
help apropos > metadata.out
printf '%s\n' 'apropos builtin help available'

cases.purpose: After the reference dependency is available, compare GNU default regular-expression and OR semantics, -w alias matching, no-match status, and leading-dash queries against the same private whatis fixtures.
cases.reason: No man-db query comparison has been executed. The old blocker (/etc/manpath.config missing) is stale: the VM reference image installs man-db 2.13.1. The real gap is a fixture that builds a private man-db index for the reference side. The candidate also lacks regex, OR and glob semantics, so parity is expected to fail.
